blogs.title: Why Your AI Model is Too Big to Train: Enter Orthogonal Butterfly (BOFT)
blogs.description: This post breaks down the core problem of 'foundation model' bloat—why training massive models like LLMs from scratch is impossible for most—and introduces BOFT as the solution. We'll explore how BOFT adapts these giant models to your specific tasks using a fraction of the parameters, making advanced AI accessible without needing a supercomputer.

blogs.title: From FFT to Finetuning: How Math's Fastest Algorithm Saves Parameters
blogs.description: Dive into the fascinating intersection of signal processing and machine learning. Learn how the Cooley-Tukey Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) algorithm inspired a new way to build orthogonal matrices. We'll demystify 'butterfly structures' and show how they allow us to create complex, dense transformations using surprisingly few numbers.

blogs.title: Preserving Knowledge: Why Keeping Neurons at Right Angles Matters
blogs.description: Unlike standard fine-tuning which risks 'forgetting' what a model learned during pre-training, Orthogonal Finetuning ensures that the geometric relationships between neurons remain intact. This article explains the science behind preserving 'pairwise angles,' why it leads to better stability, and how BOFT takes this concept even further by enabling denser, more flexible transformations.

blogs.title: The Information Highway: Visualizing Matrix Factorization as Data Transmission
blogs.description: Imagine sending data across a grid where you want everyone to talk to everyone else efficiently. We visualize the challenge of creating dense orthogonal matrices through an 'information transmission' lens. Discover how arranging sparse connections in a specific 'butterfly' pattern allows information to flow globally while keeping the cost (parameters) incredibly low.
